name: Zedekiah (son of Josiah)
title: Judah's last king
summary: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah before Babylon's destruction of Jerusalem. He was installed as a vassal king by Nebuchadnezzar, but his rebellion against Babylon led to the fall of Jerusalem and the temple's destruction in 586 BC. His reign was marked by weakness and disobedience to God's word through the prophet Jeremiah.

keyEvents.title: Installed as king by Nebuchadnezzar
keyEvents.description: Nebuchadnezzar installed Zedekiah as king over Judah after taking Jehoiachin captive to Babylon. He was twenty-one years old when he became king and reigned for eleven years.

keyEvents.title: Did what was evil in the Lord's sight
keyEvents.description: Zedekiah did not follow the Lord's will and refused to humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke the Lord's words to him.

keyEvents.title: Secret conversations with Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Zedekiah sought counsel from Jeremiah in secret on several occasions but lacked the courage to follow the prophet's advice to surrender to the Babylonians.

keyEvents.title: Rebellion against Babylon
keyEvents.description: Zedekiah broke his oath to Nebuchadnezzar and rebelled by seeking help from Egypt, which led to Babylon's siege of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The fall of Jerusalem and Zedekiah's flight
keyEvents.description: When the city fell, Zedekiah fled at night but was captured on the plains of Jericho. He was brought before Nebuchadnezzar in Ribla for judgment.

keyEvents.title: Zedekiah's terrible fate
keyEvents.description: Nebuchadnezzar had Zedekiah's sons killed before his eyes, then he blinded him and took him in chains to Babylon, where he died.
